investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler with "Unschedulable: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector." No VM was ever allocated, so the eval runner never received orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState, causing all four required evidence fields to be absent and every contract assertion to fail.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has exhausted the schedulable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the two nodes that match the pod's node affinity/selector. Of the 6 total nodes, 4 do not satisfy the pod's affinity rules and are therefore ineligible, and the remaining 2 eligible nodes report "Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm" — meaning the peer-pod VM quota on those nodes is fully consumed. Preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist. The eval runner's createAgent call (run-status-probes.mjs line 1885) never progresses past pod scheduling, so no VM ID or remote state is ever returned, and the expected-output contract (check-expectations.json line 256–259) is violated in full. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the two affinity-eligible nodes: concurrent remote agent workloads or leaked/zombie peer-pod VMs have consumed all available VM slots, leaving no capacity for new scheduling attempts. Preemption is blocked because no lower-priority pods exist on those nodes.

SECONDARY — Node affinity/selector misconfiguration or node pool shrinkage: 4 of 6 nodes are permanently ineligible due to affinity rules, reducing the effective scheduling domain to only 2 nodes. If those 2 nodes were recently cordoned, drained, or had their kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable value reduced, capacity would drop to zero.

TERTIARY — Leaked or stuck peer-pod VMs from prior eval runs not being cleaned up: the withCleanup wrapper in run-status-probes.mjs (line 1883) is responsible for teardown; if prior runs failed before cleanup executed, orphaned VM allocations could be holding the kata.peerpods.io/vm quota on the eligible nodes.

Add a historical pass/fail trend eval for remote-agent-create so that regressions from a passing baseline are detected immediately; the current run history shows previousRunCount=0 and lastPassingAt=null, making trend analysis impossible.

The eval runner's createAgent call (run-status-probes.mjs line 1918) never returned a live agent, so the probe timed out after ~142–143 seconds and returned an empty evidence object, failing all five required-evidence assertions. This is an eval-infrastructure / cluster-capacity failure localized to the remote-agents swarm in production-api; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler with "Unschedulable: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector." No VM was ever allocated, so the eval runner never received orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState, causing all four required evidence fields to be absent and every contract assertion to fail.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has exhausted the schedulable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the two nodes that match the pod's node affinity/selector. Of the 6 total nodes, 4 do not satisfy the pod's affinity rules and are therefore ineligible, and the remaining 2 eligible nodes report "Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm" — meaning the peer-pod VM quota on those nodes is fully consumed. Preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist. The eval runner's createAgent call (run-status-probes.mjs line 1885) never progresses past pod scheduling, so no VM ID or remote state is ever returned, and the expected-output contract (check-expectations.json line 256–259) is violated in full. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical scheduler rejection message, pod stuck for 142s, latencyMs=146709

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf ['running','idle','ready']; neither assertion can be evaluated when the pod never starts
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=140299 (approx 140s), consistent with the scheduler's 134s unschedulable window reported in the message before the probe timed out
possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the two affinity-eligible nodes: concurrent remote agent workloads or leaked/zombie peer-pod VMs have consumed all available VM slots, leaving no capacity for new scheduling attempts. Preemption is blocked because no lower-priority pods exist on those nodes.

SECONDARY — Node affinity/selector misconfiguration or node pool shrinkage: 4 of 6 nodes are permanently ineligible due to affinity rules, reducing the effective scheduling domain to only 2 nodes. If those 2 nodes were recently cordoned, drained, or had their kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable value reduced, capacity would drop to zero.

TERTIARY — Leaked or stuck peer-pod VMs from prior eval runs not being cleaned up: the withCleanup wrapper in run-status-probes.mjs (line 1883) is responsible for teardown; if prior runs failed before cleanup executed, orphaned VM allocations could be holding the kata.peerpods.io/vm quota on the eligible nodes.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes Swarm Nodes Exhausted of kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted by the eval runner was stuck unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource were fully exhausted, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No agent was ever created, so the eval produced zero evidence and violated every field of the expected-output contract (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message).
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents swarm had insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity at the time of the eval run. With 0/6 nodes available — 2 reporting "Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm" and 4 not matching the pod's node affinity/selector — no remote agent pod could be scheduled. The eval runner's createAgent call (run-status-probes.mjs line 1918) never returned a live agent, so the probe timed out after ~142–143 seconds and returned an empty evidence object, failing all five required-evidence assertions. This is an eval-infrastructure / cluster-capacity failure localized to the remote-agents swarm in production-api; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: all available VM slots were consumed by existing pods at the time of the eval run, leaving no capacity for the eval's agent pod. Preemption was also unavailable ('No preemption victims found'), meaning no lower-priority pod could be evicted to make room.

SECONDARY — Node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy, and those 2 were already at capacity. If the affinity configuration is overly restrictive or the eligible node pool has not scaled out, any demand spike will exhaust capacity.

TERTIARY — Cluster autoscaler did not provision a new node in time: if autoscaling is configured for the kata.peerpods.io/vm node pool, it may not have responded within the eval's timeout window (~142s), causing the probe to fail before a new node became ready.

LOWER — Transient spike in concurrent remote agent creation: if other workloads or concurrent eval runs were also requesting kata.peerpods.io/vm slots simultaneously, the resource pool could have been temporarily exhausted without a persistent capacity deficit.
